contexts.text: Man is born into no exercise of life, as brute animals are; but he learns everything; and the things he learns acquire habit from exercise...
The soul is in the use and the end, and the body is in the exercise of them.
The spiritual man is in his bliss... still more when he is in the exercise of good according to truths; nor does he spurn wealth, because he can thereby be in exercise.
His herds = the exercises of charity; (for) herds = the exterior goods of charity; thus the exercises of it...
By worship according to the order of Heaven, is meant all the exercise of good according to the Lord's precepts.
He who does good for the sake of good... exercises charity.
No one can be withheld from evil... unless by means of the exercise of charity in the world he has received that capacity.
The exercise of charity is signified by to lend. Illustrated.
The exercises of charity... can exist in proportion as man has business to do.
In a series of like degrees are will, understanding, and exercise; for... exercise is of use and thence of work.
It appears as though in use, action, work, and exercise, there is no more than such as there is in motion; yet all the prior things are actually in them; and that so fully that nothing is wanting...
Such are faith and charity without their exercises.
Charity is exercised towards them in different ways...
Love towards the neighbour and its exercise towards man in the singular and towards man in the plural. Explained.
A priest... eminently exercises charity.
Justice and fidelity form his mind; and their exercises his body.
Through exercises imbues charity.
That in the exercises of charity man does not place merit in works when...
For the exercises of moral life and of charity are the same.
They had exercised this in the life of the body...
In the life of the body had studied... in thought, and in clandestine exercise to destroy others.
Therefore their love towards the neighbour also consists in exercises, which are works.
According to the quality and quantity of the cupidity of domineering and its exercise...
